entries.title: II Samuel 18:1
segments: ¶And David numbered the people that [were] with him, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over them.

entries.title: II Samuel 18:2
segments: And David sent forth a third part of the people under the hand of Joab, and a third part under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and a third part under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said unto the people, I will surely go forth with you myself also.

entries.title: II Samuel 18:3
segments: But the people answered, Thou shalt not go forth: for if we flee away, they will not care for us; neither if half of us die, will they care for us: but now [thou art] worth ten thousand of us: therefore now [it is] better that thou succour us out of the city. {care...: Heb. set their heart on us} {worth...: Heb. as ten thousand of us} {succour: Heb. be to succour or help}

words.text: for us: but now [thou art] worth
of us: therefore now [it is] better
. {care...: Heb. set their heart on us} {worth...: Heb. as ten thousand of us} {succour: Heb. be to succour or help}

entries.title: II Samuel 18:4
segments: And the king said unto them, What seemeth you best I will do. And the king stood by the gate side, and all the people came out by hundreds and by thousands.

entries.title: II Samuel 18:5
segments: And the king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, [Deal] gently for my sake with the young man, [even] with Absalom. And all the people heard when the king gave all the captains charge concerning Absalom.

words.text: for my sake with the young man

entries.title: II Samuel 18:6
segments: So the people went out into the field against Israel: and the battle was in the wood of Ephraim;

entries.title: II Samuel 18:7
segments: Where the people of Israel were slain before the servants of David, and there was there a great slaughter that day of twenty thousand [men].

words.text: , and there was there a great

entries.title: II Samuel 18:8
segments: For the battle was there scattered over the face of all the country: and the wood devoured more people that day than the sword devoured. {devoured: Heb. multiplied to devour}

entries.title: II Samuel 18:9
segments: ¶And Absalom met the servants of David. And Absalom rode upon a mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of a great oak, and his head caught hold of the oak, and he was taken up between the heaven and the earth; and the mule that [was] under him went away.

entries.title: II Samuel 18:10
segments: And a certain man saw [it], and told Joab, and said, Behold, I saw Absalom hanged in an oak.

entries.title: II Samuel 18:11
segments: And Joab said unto the man that told him, And, behold, thou sawest [him], and why didst thou not smite him there to the ground? and I would have given thee ten [shekels] of silver, and a girdle.

words.text: [him], and why didst thou not smite

entries.title: II Samuel 18:12
segments: And the man said unto Joab, Though I should receive a thousand [shekels] of silver in mine hand, [yet] would I not put forth mine hand against the king's son: for in our hearing the king charged thee and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Beware that none [touch] the young man Absalom. {receive: Heb. weigh upon mine hand} {Beware...: Heb. Beware whosoever ye be of, etc}

words.text: . {receive: Heb. weigh upon mine hand} {Beware...: Heb. Beware whosoever ye be of, etc}

entries.title: II Samuel 18:13
segments: Otherwise I should have wrought falsehood against mine own life: for there is no matter hid from the king, and thou thyself wouldest have set thyself against [me].

words.text: , and thou thyself wouldest have set

entries.title: II Samuel 18:14
segments: Then said Joab, I may not tarry thus with thee. And he took three darts in his hand, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom, while he [was] yet alive in the midst of the oak. {with...: Heb. before thee} {midst: Heb. heart}

words.text: in the midst of the oak

entries.title: II Samuel 18:15
segments: And ten young men that bare Joab's armour compassed about and smote Absalom, and slew him.

entries.title: II Samuel 18:16
segments: And Joab blew the trumpet, and the people returned from pursuing after Israel: for Joab held back the people.

entries.title: II Samuel 18:17
segments: And they took Absalom, and cast him into a great pit in the wood, and laid a very great heap of stones upon him: and all Israel fled every one to his tent.

entries.title: II Samuel 18:18
segments: Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself a pillar, which [is] in the king's dale: for he said, I have no son to keep my name in remembrance: and he called the pillar after his own name: and it is called unto this day, Absalom's place.

entries.title: II Samuel 18:19
segments: ¶Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok, Let me now run, and bear the king tidings, how that the LORD hath avenged him of his enemies. {avenged...: Heb. judged him from the hand, etc}

words.text: . {avenged...: Heb. judged him from the hand, etc}

entries.title: II Samuel 18:20
segments: And Joab said unto him, Thou shalt not bear tidings this day, but thou shalt bear tidings another day: but this day thou shalt bear no tidings, because the king's son is dead. {bear tidings this: Heb. be a man of tidings, etc}

words.text: . {bear tidings this: Heb. be a man of tidings, etc}

entries.title: II Samuel 18:21
segments: Then said Joab to Cushi, Go tell the king what thou hast seen. And Cushi bowed himself unto Joab, and ran.

entries.title: II Samuel 18:22
segments: Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok yet again to Joab, But howsoever, let me, I pray thee, also run after Cushi. And Joab said, Wherefore wilt thou run, my son, seeing that thou hast no tidings ready? {howsoever: Heb. be what may} {ready: or, convenient}

entries.title: II Samuel 18:23
segments: But howsoever, [said he], let me run. And he said unto him, Run. Then Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain, and overran Cushi.

words.text: But howsoever, [said he], let me run

entries.title: II Samuel 18:24
segments: And David sat between the two gates: and the watchman went up to the roof over the gate unto the wall, and lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold a man running alone.

entries.title: II Samuel 18:25
segments: And the watchman cried, and told the king. And the king said, If he [be] alone, [there is] tidings in his mouth. And he came apace, and drew near.

entries.title: II Samuel 18:26
segments: And the watchman saw another man running: and the watchman called unto the porter, and said, Behold [another] man running alone. And the king said, He also bringeth tidings.

entries.title: II Samuel 18:27
segments: And the watchman said, Me thinketh the running of the foremost is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok. And the king said, He [is] a good man, and cometh with good tidings. {Me...: Heb. I see the running}

entries.title: II Samuel 18:28
segments: And Ahimaaz called, and said unto the king, All is well. And he fell down to the earth upon his face before the king, and said, Blessed [be] the LORD thy God, which hath delivered up the men that lifted up their hand against my lord the king. {All...: or, Peace be to thee: Heb. Peace} {delivered...: Heb. shut up}

words.text: . {All...: or, Peace be to thee: Heb. Peace} {delivered...: Heb. shut up}

entries.title: II Samuel 18:29
segments: And the king said, Is the young man Absalom safe? And Ahimaaz answered, When Joab sent the king's servant, and [me] thy servant, I saw a great tumult, but I knew not what [it was]. {Is...: Heb. Is there peace?}

words.text: not what [it was]. {Is...: Heb. Is there peace?}

entries.title: II Samuel 18:30
segments: And the king said [unto him], Turn aside, [and] stand here. And he turned aside, and stood still.

entries.title: II Samuel 18:31
segments: And, behold, Cushi came; and Cushi said, Tidings, my lord the king: for the LORD hath avenged thee this day of all them that rose up against thee. {Tidings: Heb. Tidings is brought}

words.text: against thee. {Tidings: Heb. Tidings is brought}

entries.title: II Samuel 18:32
segments: And the king said unto Cushi, Is the young man Absalom safe? And Cushi answered, The enemies of my lord the king, and all that rise against thee to do [thee] hurt, be as [that] young man [is].

entries.title: II Samuel 18:33
segments: And the king was much moved, and went up to the chamber over the gate, and wept: and as he went, thus he said, O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! would God I had died for thee, O Absalom, my son, my son!
